sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic PR #11 At-usability outcome at head b2eb3ac0b
sapience_notes.value: Making an `abbrev` like `At` usable in tactic proofs took a `@[simp] at_def` lemma, but the measured result is narrower than 'At now rewrites': the working idiom is a three-lemma `simp only [at_def, TruthEnv.T, <language clause lemma>]`, and `rw` to a per-language clause lemma under `At` still fails because that lemma is stated about the instance projection, which must be reduced first. `at_def` is load-bearing (omitting it leaves `simp` with no progress) on the language-specific route and reported unused on a generic clause former, where `simp` already sees through the reducible `At`.

sapience_notes.subject: Lake .trace files key on absolute source paths
sapience_notes.value: Seeding a Lean review worktree's `.lake/build` by copying another worktree's produces a false green: Lake's per-module `.trace` records the absolute source path of the worktree it was built in and re-hashes that path, so a module whose source differs between the two worktrees is judged up to date and never rebuilt. The symptom is a green build in which the file under review has no fresh `.olean`; the audit is `grep -rl '<other worktree path>' .lake/build/lib/lean --include='*.trace'` returning 0, and the remedy is wiping `.lake/build` (`.lake/packages` may still be shared by symlink).

sapience_notes.subject: lake-build-guard.sh --dir does not chdir
sapience_notes.value: The `--dir` flag resolves the Lean project root for locking and result-record paths only; the wrapped `lake` still runs in the caller's cwd. Invoking the guard from a main repository with `--dir <worktree>` therefore builds the main repository and writes a green result into the worktree's guard files, and the guard will then REPLAY that result for a later worktree call whose fingerprint matches. Always `cd` into the project you mean to build, and clear a stale `.lake/build-guard.result` first.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh scope under a multi-task orchestrate batch
sapience_notes.value: verify-touched.sh derives touched paths from the whole working tree plus the committed diff against its own determined base, not from the calling task's own modified_files. Under a multi-task batch it therefore picks up sibling dispatches' and prior sessions' changes: a task touching only four files under specs/** selected 91 suites and ran 95. A resulting failure is not automatically the calling task's; attribution has to be checked against that task's own modified_files before treating a scoped run's red as this task's red.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic test-deploy-baseline-lib.sh warm-cache control failure is standing
sapience_notes.value: The case 'control: a genuinely matching warm-cache entry was expected to skip gate 1 but did not' fails reproducibly and is owned by no task. It is a defect in verify-deploy.sh's gate-cache warm-path logic itself, confirmed in freshly created isolated scratch directories, so it is not a concurrency artifact of a shared specs/.gate-cache. Every scoped or full battery run in this repository will keep reporting exactly one NEW failure until it is fixed or marked expected.

sapience_notes.subject: Splitting re-review measurement from re-review prose
sapience_notes.value: Pinning a PR head sha in the research artifact and making the implementation phase's first action a re-probe against that pin turned a PR re-review into a near-mechanical prose dispatch: two `gh pr view` probes (5 minutes apart, both byte-identical) validated the carried measurement instead of re-running a from-scratch worktree build. The pin doubles as a hard stop condition, so a moved head blocks rather than silently producing an approval of unmeasured code.
